name: unanimous_synthesis_approval
description: All producers return correct answers, all judges classify every candidate as CORRECT, and all selected non-leader evaluators approve the leader's synthesis; every transaction is finalized as SYNTHESIZED.

transactions.prompt: What are the trade-offs between stack and heap allocation in systems programming?
Why is immutability important for concurrent data structures?
How does a blockchain validator verify a proposed block before signing?

answers.mr3-s01-control-before: Stack allocation is deterministic and fast but size-limited; heap allocation supports dynamic sizes at the cost of explicit management or garbage collection overhead.
answers.mr3-s01-scenario-target: Immutable data structures cannot be modified after creation, so concurrent readers never observe partial updates and locks are unnecessary.
answers.mr3-s01-control-after: A validator re-executes all transactions, verifies every signature, recomputes body and header hashes, and checks that the previous-block hash links to the known chain tip.

answers.mr3-s01-control-before: Stack allocation offers predictable, fast memory reuse without fragmentation but is constrained by frame size; heap allocation provides unbounded dynamic sizing at the cost of explicit deallocation or garbage-collector pauses and potential fragmentation.
answers.mr3-s01-scenario-target: Immutability eliminates the possibility of concurrent modification, making shared state safe to read from multiple goroutines without locks and preventing entire classes of data races.
answers.mr3-s01-control-after: A validator reconstructs the block by re-executing every transaction, verifying each transaction and block signature against known public keys, recomputing body and header hashes, and confirming the previous-block hash correctly extends the local chain.

finalAnswers.answer: Stack allocation offers predictable, fast memory reuse without fragmentation but is constrained by frame size; heap allocation provides unbounded dynamic sizing at the cost of explicit deallocation or garbage-collector pauses and potential fragmentation.
Immutability eliminates the possibility of concurrent modification, making shared state safe to read from multiple goroutines without locks and preventing entire classes of data races.

A validator reconstructs the block by re-executing every transaction, verifying each transaction and block signature against known public keys, recomputing body and header hashes, and confirming the previous-block hash correctly extends the local chain.
